name: Barbell Romanian Deadlift
machineIdentification: A barbell, ideally taken from a rack at hip height so you don't have to deadlift it off the floor first.
instructions: Stand holding a barbell at your hips, feet hip width.
Soften your knees and keep them fixed there.
Push your hips back, letting the bar slide down your thighs.
Stop when you feel a strong hamstring stretch, bar around shin height.
Drive your hips forward to stand tall.
keyCues: Keep the bar in contact with your legs the whole way.
Push your hips back rather than bending your knees.
Keep your back flat — chest proud.
commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back at the bottom.
Turning it into a squat by bending the knees.
Letting the bar drift away from the legs.

name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
instructions: Hold a dumbbell in each hand in front of your thighs.
Stand feet hip width with knees softly bent.
Push your hips back and lower the dumbbells down your legs.
Stop at a strong hamstring stretch, around mid-shin.
Squeeze your glutes to return to standing.
keyCues: Keep the dumbbells close to your legs.
Hinge at the hips, not the waist.
Keep your neck in line with your spine.
commonMistakes: Bending the knees more as you descend.
Rounding the upper back to reach lower.
Hyperextending the back at the top.

name: Cable Pull-Through
machineIdentification: A cable pulley set at the lowest position with a rope attached. You stand facing away from the tower with the rope between your legs.
instructions: Set a pulley at the bottom and attach a rope.
Face away from the tower and reach between your legs for the rope.
Step forward until the cable is taut, feet shoulder width.
Hinge at the hips, letting the rope travel back between your legs.
Snap your hips forward to stand tall and squeeze your glutes.
keyCues: Drive the hips forward — the arms just hold the rope.
Keep your back flat throughout.
Finish with a hard glute squeeze, not a back arch.
commonMistakes: Pulling the rope with the arms like a row.
Squatting down instead of hinging back.
Leaning back at the top and arching the lower back.

name: Kettlebell Swing
instructions: Stand with a kettlebell on the floor a foot in front of you.
Hinge at the hips and grip the handle with both hands.
Hike the bell back between your legs.
Snap your hips forward to swing it up to chest height.
Let it fall back between your legs and repeat.
keyCues: The hips throw the bell — the arms are just rope.
Snap your glutes hard at the top.
Keep the bell above your knees on the backswing.
commonMistakes: Lifting the bell with the shoulders like a front raise.
Squatting the bell up and down instead of hinging.
Letting the lower back round on the backswing.

name: Conventional Deadlift
machineIdentification: A loaded barbell on the floor. Standard plates put the bar at the right starting height; use blocks if you're using smaller plates.
instructions: Stand with the bar over your mid-foot, feet hip width.
Hinge down and grip the bar just outside your legs.
Drop your hips until your shins touch the bar, chest up.
Push the floor away and stand, keeping the bar against your legs.
Lower it back down by pushing your hips back.
keyCues: Take the slack out of the bar before you pull.
Keep the bar dragging up your shins and thighs.
Finish standing tall, not leaning back.
commonMistakes: Yanking the bar off the floor with a rounded back.
Letting the hips rise before the bar moves.
Hyperextending the lower back at lockout.

name: Back Extension
machineIdentification: An angled or horizontal frame with a pad for your hips and rollers to hook your ankles under. You hang forward from the hips and lift back up.
instructions: Set the hip pad just below your hip bones.
Hook your ankles under the rollers.
Cross your arms over your chest.
Hinge down until your torso is near vertical.
Squeeze your glutes to lift back to a straight line.
keyCues: Stop when your body is straight — don't arch past it.
Lead the lift with your glutes, not your lower back.
Round your upper back slightly to bias the glutes.
commonMistakes: Swinging up and hyperextending at the top.
Setting the pad too high, which blocks the hinge.
Rushing the reps with momentum.

name: Seated Leg Curl Machine
machineIdentification: A seat with a padded roller that sits across the backs of your ankles and a thigh pad that clamps down over your legs.
instructions: Set the back pad so your knees line up with the pivot.
Sit with your legs straight over the ankle roller.
Pull the thigh pad down snug across your legs.
Curl your heels down and back underneath the seat.
Return slowly to straight legs.
keyCues: Keep your hips flat in the seat.
Squeeze for a beat at the bottom of the curl.
Take three seconds to return.
commonMistakes: Lifting the hips to help the curl.
Letting the weight snap the legs back straight.
Setting the thigh pad loose so the legs shift.

name: Lying Leg Curl Machine
machineIdentification: A bench you lie face-down on, with a padded roller at the far end that sits across the backs of your ankles.
instructions: Lie face down with your knees just past the edge of the pad.
Hook your ankles under the roller.
Grip the handles under the bench.
Curl your heels toward your glutes.
Lower slowly until your legs are straight.
keyCues: Keep your hips pressed into the bench.
Point your toes toward your shins.
Pause at the top of each curl.
commonMistakes: Lifting the hips off the bench to swing the weight.
Only curling halfway.
Letting the stack drop back fast.

name: Stability Ball Hamstring Curl
machineIdentification: A large inflatable stability ball, usually stored in the stretching area.
instructions: Lie on your back with your heels on top of the ball.
Lift your hips so your body forms a straight line.
Pull the ball toward your glutes by bending your knees.
Straighten your legs slowly to roll it back out.
keyCues: Keep your hips high the entire set.
Move slowly — speed makes it easier, not harder.
Use one leg to make it considerably harder.
commonMistakes: Letting the hips drop as the ball rolls out.
Rushing so momentum does the work.
Bridging with the glutes instead of curling with the hamstrings.

name: Seated Calf Raise Machine
machineIdentification: A seat with a pad that clamps down across your thighs and a small foot platform below. You press up onto your toes against the thigh pad.
instructions: Sit and place the balls of your feet on the platform.
Lower the thigh pad snug across your knees.
Release the safety catch.
Press up onto your toes as high as you can.
Lower your heels below the platform for a full stretch.
keyCues: Pause for a beat at the top of every rep.
Get a deep stretch at the bottom.
Slow reps beat heavy ones here.
commonMistakes: Bouncing through a very short range.
Skipping the stretch at the bottom.
Going so heavy the range collapses to inches.

name: Standing Calf Raise Machine
machineIdentification: A standing frame with shoulder pads above and a raised foot block below, so your heels can drop past the edge.
instructions: Set the shoulder pads so you stand slightly crouched under them.
Place the balls of your feet on the block, heels hanging off.
Stand up to take the load onto your shoulders.
Press up onto your toes as high as possible.
Lower your heels below the block for a deep stretch.
keyCues: Keep your knees straight but not locked.
Full range: all the way down, all the way up.
Hold the top position for a second.
commonMistakes: Bending the knees to bounce the weight up.
Using a tiny range of motion.
Rushing so the calves never actually stretch.

name: Leg Press Calf Raise
machineIdentification: The leg press machine, but with your feet low on the platform so only the balls of your feet make contact.
instructions: Sit in the leg press with feet low on the platform.
Press the sled out and leave the safeties engaged.
Straighten your legs but keep a soft knee bend.
Push the platform away using only your ankles.
Let your heels travel back toward you for a stretch.
keyCues: Keep the safety catches on — this is not a full press.
Keep the knees still; only the ankles move.
Pause at full extension each rep.
commonMistakes: Bending the knees and turning it into a leg press.
Letting the feet slip off the bottom of the platform.
Releasing the safeties, which is unnecessary and risky.
